Deck.et: From Dutch dek. Borrowed via German Low German Deck and hence with a plural in -s (Dutch uses dekken). The older Low German form is preserved in Verdeck. Cognate with English deck.

s: any cloth or cushion used as a covering; a tablecloth, blanket, quilt, duvet, etc.
ceiling (surface at the upper limit of a room or cavity)
Mir fällt die Decke auf den Kopf.
I am suffering from cabin fever
Decke.et:
From Middle High German decke, from Old High German theckī, decchī, derived from thecken (modern decken), from Proto-West Germanic *þakkjan, from Proto-Germanic *þakjaną.
Cognate with English deck. Compare analogous Dutch dek. Also related with German Dach, Du…

Deckenfluter.et: From Decke (“ceiling”) and fluten (“to flood”). So named because the ceiling is "flooded" with light by this kind of lamp.

s: to cover (a roof, with a blanket, etc.)
to cover (e.g. a demand, a loss; but not “to provide news coverage”)
decken.et:
From Middle High German decken, from Old High German decchen, from Proto-West Germanic *þakkjan. Equivalent to Dach + -en.
Cognate with West Frisian dekke, Dutch dekken, English thatch, Danish tække, Swedish täcka.

s: to decipher (to decode or decrypt a code or cipher)
lid, cap (the cover of a container)
Deckel.et: From Middle High German deckel, equivalent to decken + -el. Cognate with Middle Low German deckel (“lid, covering”).

s: stud, stallion (male horse kept for breeding)

Dechsel.et: From Middle High German dehsele, from Old High German dehsala, thehsala, from Proto-West Germanic *þehsulā, from Proto-Germanic *þehsulǭ (“axe”). Cognate with Dutch dissel, Old Norse þexla.

Dechant.et:
From Middle High German dechant, techant, from Old High German tehhant, tehhan, from Proto-West Germanic *dekan (“deacon”), from Latin decanus (“dean”). Doublet of Dekan, a 15th-century borrowing.
In Middle Low German dēken, the full vowel in the second syllab…

deckungsschädlich.et: Deckung + -s- + schädlich (“preclusive for a right to arise”)

s: deca, the anabolic steroid nandrolone decanoate.

Deckennetzspinne.et: By surface analysis, Decke (“cover-cloth”) + -n- + Netz (“net”) + Spinne (“spider”).

t: Weltflucht heißt gewöhnlich nicht „Tischlein, deck dich“.
Escapism doesn't usually put food on the table.
Ist es die Decke mit dem Wellenmuster?
Is it the blanket with the wavy pattern?
Sie wickelte sich in eine Decke ein.
She wrapped herself in a blanket.
Bedecken Sie den Verletzten mit dieser Decke.
Cover up the injured man with this blanket.
l: Doch die Pläne decken sich nicht mit den Wünschen der Berufsfeuerwehr Braunschweig.
Helene muss sich entscheiden, ob sie Günthers Lüge decken soll oder nicht.
Rostige Körbe an der Decke sollen an die Bergbau-Vergangenheit der Stadt erinnern.
b: Hernach wurden zwei schöne Bettlein weiß gedeckt, und Hänsel und Grethel legten sich hinein und meinten sie wären im Himmel.
然后两张漂亮的小床铺上了白床单，亨塞尔和格蕾特躺进去，以为自己在天堂里。
